steps.c: This grid is not made for your field. It is one fixed grid over the whole world. It starts with 6 giant cells, like the faces of a cube blown up into a ball.
Each of them is cut into 4, and again: 24 cells at level 1, 96 at level 2. Every cell of every level has its fixed place, worked out in advance.
Zoomed in on Europe: level 4. Each cell is about 332,074 km². The orange one contains Munich.
Level 6, about 20,755 km² per cell. Two more cuts turned each level-4 cell into 16 of these. Munich happens to lie close to the edge of its cell.
Level 8, about 1,297 km² per cell, roughly a city.
Level 10, about 81 km² per cell. Three more cuts give level 13, about 1.3 km², the smallest cells used for MU. Next: those smallest cells in Munich.
